name: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome
definition: Compression or irritation of neurovascular structures traversing the thoracic outlet; neurogenic TOS is most common, while venous and arterial forms require distinct urgent pathways.

typical: Vascular swelling/color change suggests vascular TOS

investigations.MRI: MRI/vascular imaging or electrodiagnostics are selected according to suspected subtype.
investigations.radiographs: Chest/cervical radiographs may identify cervical rib.

green: Postural/scapular and breathing rehabilitation for selected neurogenic cases
amber: Vascular TOS or progressive neurological deficit needs specialist assessment; thrombosis is urgent.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Upper-limb Vata/neuromuscular phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Compression or irritation of neurovascular structures traversing the thoracic outlet; neurogenic TOS is most common, while venous and arterial forms require distinct urgent pathways.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for severe/progressive neurological deficit, vascular compromise, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
